public.app-category.productivity

When you click Go to on a coding agent, SparkV selects its tab in Terminal or iTerm2. SparkV reads the current track from Music and Spotify and sends play, pause and skip commands to them. When you ask, it also favorites the track, changes shuffle and repeat, adds the song to a Music playlist, reads lyrics saved in Music, and reads the Spotify track id so a connected Spotify account can save it. When you choose Save to Spaces, it reads the open page from Safari, Chrome, Arc, Edge or Brave, or the selected message in Mail. The Job Agent reads the address and title of the job page you capture with fn + Control. During Focus, it reads the address of the front browser tab to spot sites you chose to block. During a Mode, SparkV opens your chosen music in its own Safari window (or plays a playlist in Music) and closes only that window when the mode ends, and switches between light and dark appearance through System Events.

SparkV shows your AirPods and headphones' battery when they connect, lists paired headphones in Sound Output so you can connect and switch to them, and connects them when you tap AirPods in the quick toggles.
SparkV shows your next meeting under the notch with a one-click Join button.
SparkV shows your reminders due today in the notch, lets you tick them off and add new ones, and adds the meeting tasks you choose. Nothing is changed unless you click.

SparkV listens to what your Mac plays while Ambient Light or Live Level Bars are on, so the notch can glow and move with your music, and passes an app's sound through at the level you set in App Volumes. The sound is processed on this Mac and never recorded or sent anywhere.

SparkV uses the camera you choose (the built-in FaceTime HD camera, an external webcam or a Continuity Camera iPhone) for the private mirror preview, to warn you when you sit too close to the screen (Screen Distance, if you turn it on) and, if you set it up, to recognize your face and unlock your Mac. Video is processed on-device and never leaves your Mac.
SparkV saves your screen recordings to the Desktop and moves a download there when you sort it there.
SparkV moves a download into your Documents folder when you sort it there.
SparkV shows download progress under the notch and helps you sort finished downloads. Files only move when you choose a folder or turn on an auto-sort rule.
SparkV keeps a SparkV folder in iCloud Drive up to date so you can read your meetings and notes on your iPhone.

SparkV looks for devices running LocalSend on your network while the Nearby Share panel is open, so you can send Tray files to Android, Windows and Linux. It sends only the files you pick, and only after that device accepts.
SparkV listens while you dictate, ask Clicky, record a meeting or narrate a screen recording, and turns your speech into text on this Mac.
SparkV transcribes dictation, Clicky questions and meetings with on-device speech recognition. Audio is never sent off your Mac.
